title: cross-functional-roadmap-sync-prep-apr-2026-draft
content:
Goal: prep notes for cross-functional roadmap alignment sync (Product + Eng + Applied ML). Focus: Hosted API features, latency/cost tradeoffs, model onboarding timeline, and evals coverage. Meeting = weekly xfn sync on 2026-04-16 10:00am PT. Attendees: Priya (PM), Ethan (Eng - serving runtime), Maya (Applied ML), Diego (Console/Product), plus optional: Samira (SRE), Lucas (Solutions Eng)

Agenda (30-40m):
- 5m: quick status + key metrics (priors: latency P50/P95, cost per token, request volume)
- 10m: Product priorities for Hosted API (model catalog, streaming improvements, function calling ergonomics)
- 10m: Eng constraints and risk surface (kernel support, quantization rollout, infra capacity)
- 5m: Applied ML asks (eval coverage, quality SLOs, rollout gating criteria)
- 5m: Action items + next steps

Prep notes / context:
- Q2 goals: reduce per-token cost by 15% for common chat path, maintain P95 latency under 450ms for 99% of requests.
- Recent incidents: two brief latency spikes during peak on 2026-04-06 tied to large batched KV cache misses (INF-4202). Eng fix in progress (PR linked).
- Model onboarding: plan to add rdx-2.1 and rdx-chat-2.1 (quantized variants) to Hosted catalog by end of May. Applied ML needs time to run evals vs current baselines.
- Evals: Maya requests 3 canonical prompt suites for canary gating: customer-support, code-assist, and content-moderation. Need to standardize metrics (BLEU-like? prefer custom quality score + hallucination rate + safety flags).

Open questions to raise in sync:
1) Can Eng commit to model onboarding timeline (runnable on current kernel stack) by 2026-05-28? If not, what are blockers?
2) Does Product accept temporary higher cost on new quantized models during canary (to collect metrics) or prefer cold rollout with strict cost caps?
3) Applied ML: what minimum eval pass rate do we require to mark canary->general rollout? Proposed: >=95% on quality score and lower hallucination than baseline by 10%.
4) Console: will rollouts need additional UI flags for canary buckets and observability traces? Diego to confirm capacity and ETA.

Talking points for each attendee:
- Priya (Product): emphasize customer stories where latency spikes caused support SLAs to be missed; want predictable latency and clear rollout gating for new models. Ask for tradeoff matrix (cost vs latency vs quality) in next sync.
- Ethan (Eng): will surface kernel/quantization work, timeline for PR merge (runtime#342), and expected perf delta. Note: need 2 weeks of soak testing in staging with synthetic traffic matching 95th percentile request shapes.
- Maya (Applied ML): will outline eval plan and draft prompt suites by 2026-04-20. Wants ability to run canary evals automatically against live canary traffic samples (privacy considerations).
- Diego (Console/Product): wants per-model rollout controls in console; asks whether tracing hooks are available to correlate model variant with latency/cost on token-level.

Risks to call out:
- If kernel changes land late, onboarding slips into June and Q2 cost reduction goal may miss target.
- Eval coverage gap: if applied ML doesn't have representative prompts, quality regressions might slip through canary.
- Console rollout UX delay could make canary management manual and error-prone (human risk).

Proposed decisions to seek in meeting:
- Agree to target onboarding date for rdx-2.1 and rdx-chat-2.1: 2026-05-28 (ask Eng to confirm or propose new date).
- Consensus on canary gating metrics (Maya to propose thresholds; propose >=95% quality score; <=baseline hallucination*0.9).
- Temporary allowance for slightly higher cost during canary for the first 2 weeks only, with a hard cap (product approves if Eng provides estimated delta).

Action items (owners + due dates) - initial draft:
- Ethan: post a short note in INF slack and link PR runtime#342 + expected staging soak plan; due 2026-04-17.
- Maya: share three prompt suites and metric definitions (quality score, hallucination, safety hits); due 2026-04-20.
- Diego: confirm console flags and tracing hook requirements; estimate ETA for UI changes and backend event tagging; due 2026-04-23.
- Priya: consolidate tradeoff matrix (cost vs latency vs quality) and share a one-pager before next sync; due 2026-04-22.
- Samira (SRE, optional): run capacity check for Dedicated pools to see if burst capacity can be used during canary; due 2026-04-21.

Follow-up / Notes to self:
- Bring sample telemetry dashboards to sync: P50/P95 latency by model variant, cost-per-request, token distribution by request type.
- Remind Maya to consider synthetic vs live traffic for evals and note privacy filters required for live sampling (PII scrubbers).
- If Eng suggests longer soak, propose A/B style canary with smaller bucket (5%) to limit exposure.

Draft message to send after sync (copy to attendees):
"Thanks everyone - notes + action items will be posted to Confluence (link) and I'll create follow-up JIRA tasks for each owner. If you can't hit the proposed due dates, reply with new ETA before EOD Friday. Priority for next two weeks: model onboarding cadence, eval suites, and a minimal console rollout surface for canary management."

Quick TODO before meeting:
- Attach PR link and brief perf numbers (Ethan).
- Upload draft prompt suites (Maya).
- Export dashboard screenshots (Priya).

Misc snippets / conversational lines to use during meeting:
- "If we miss the 2-week soak, can we split the effort: kernel merge + backward-compatible flag?"
- "What's the minimal metric set we need to decide canary success? Let's avoid >7 metrics for rollout gating."
- "If cost spike > X% during canary, auto-fallback to previous model variant."

End of notes. This is a living doc - update after sync and convert to final notes + JIRA tasks.
